note: Saigon in real life: signs, menu words, places and the Saigon way of saying things. Written by Claude from general knowledge, with a few facts checked on the web (18 Nov 2026). Not checked by a speaker yet.

boards.intro: Read these on doors, walls and streets. Tap one to hear it.
items: Someone looks after your motorbike for a small fee and gives you a ticket.
“Đậu xe” is the Saigon way. Official road signs say “Cấm đỗ xe”.
On doors. The other side says “Kéo”.
Quán mở cửa lúc mấy giờ?
What time does the place open?
A Saigon word. In the north people say “cẩn thận”.
My place is in an alley.

boards.intro: What you will see on a Saigon menu, and how to ask for it.
items: Cho tôi một ly cà phê sữa đá.
A glass of iced milk coffee, please.
Cho tôi một ly cà phê đen đá, ít đường.
An iced black coffee with less sugar, please.
Cho tôi một ly bạc xỉu.
Often free, or very cheap, with a meal.
Cho tôi xin một ly trà đá.
May I have a glass of iced tea?
Sold from carts on the street.
Một ly nước mía, mang về.
One sugar-cane juice, to take away.
Cho tôi một ly sinh tố bơ.
Cho tôi một dĩa cơm tấm sườn.
A plate of broken rice with a pork chop, please.
A southern noodle soup, lighter than phở.
Cho tôi một tô hủ tiếu.
A bowl of hủ tiếu, please.
Cho tôi một ổ bánh mì thịt, không cay.
One pork bánh mì, not spicy, please.
Cho tôi hai cuốn gỏi cuốn.
Eaten dry, not as a soup.
Cho tôi một tô bún thịt nướng.
A bowl of noodles with grilled pork, please.
Say it when you order drinks.
The Saigon way to ask for the bill.

boards.intro: Places everyone knows. Use them with a driver or when you ask the way.
items: The big old market in the centre of the city.
Cho tôi tới Chợ Bến Thành.
Take me to Bến Thành Market, please.
The red-brick cathedral in the centre.
Nhà thờ Đức Bà ở đâu?
Next to the cathedral. Built from 1886 to 1891.
Bưu điện Thành phố ở kế bên Nhà thờ Đức Bà.
The Central Post Office is next to the cathedral.
Also called Dinh Thống Nhất, Reunification Palace.
Tôi muốn đi Dinh Độc Lập.
I want to go to Independence Palace.
The tallest building in Vietnam, 461 metres.
A wide walking street in the centre.
Tối nay mình đi phố đi bộ Nguyễn Huệ nha.
Let's go to Nguyễn Huệ walking street tonight.
Nhà hát Thành phố ở gần đây.
The Opera House is near here.
Nhà thờ Tân Định màu hồng.
The loud backpacker street with bars.
Cho tôi ra sân bay Tân Sơn Nhất.
Take me to Tân Sơn Nhất airport, please.

boards.intro: Same meaning, different word. Learn the Saigon word, and know the northern one when you hear it. In Saigon the letters d and gi sound like an English “y”.
items: Common in the south. Everywhere: mẹ.
My mom is in the US.
The relaxed Saigon way to say không.
Start an answer with it to sound polite.
